executive_assessment.text: The 2016 drought report describes gendered water-point tensions and child-protection risks. These are historical mechanisms, not current conflict rates.
Named Southern Lowlands and Thaba-Tseka vulnerabilities, reported restoration outputs and planned IACoV II services deepen the institutional and local picture without claiming evaluated impact.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated not stated reports: The UN reported 2025 support for restoration in degraded areas of Mafeteng, Mohale's Hoek and Quthing, including agroforestry, 400 indigenous trees and a check dam; it also reported drought anticipatory-action protocols and improved early-warning procedures for the DMA.

Source dated 2026-03-02 reports: The UN identifies Mafeteng, Mohale's Hoek and Quthing in the Southern Lowlands as facing recurrent drought and land degradation that undermine farming; Thaba-Tseka in the Highlands faces drought, erosion and limited services alongside high poverty and chronic malnutrition.

Source dated 2026-03-02 reports: Phase II plans better seasonal forecasts, gender-responsive last-mile climate services, anticipatory action, ecosystem rehabilitation, livelihood diversification and improved market links; it prioritizes women-headed households, youth, persons with disabilities and remote rural communities.

known_gaps.text: Lesotho's recent Second NDC, 2025 NAP and World Bank Climate Risk Country Profile could not be opened in this workflow; claims therefore rely on the opened drought profile and 2016 World Bank assessment summary.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
Reported protection-risk mechanism is not a measured effect on violence.
The official LVAC/IPC PDF endpoint timed out; the national food-security classifications and drivers rely on substantive official indexed PDF excerpts rather than direct full-PDF retrieval.
The 2025/2026 IPC projection period ended by the 27 October 2026 access date; this extraction does not establish the realized outcome or current food insecurity level.

The 2016 drought report gives a direct climate-to-tension mechanism but is time-bound and does not establish current conflict incidence. No reviewed source shows that FCV or insecurity blocked a named climate-adaptation activity.

The WFP independent Phase I evaluation landing page was accessible, but its linked report PDF was not; evaluation findings were not used. UN-reported project outputs and launch statements are not independent outcome evaluations.

IPC indexed excerpts excluded: the original PDF timed out. Remaining primary UN report and official launch article support named district exposure, historical water-point tensions and reported capacity outputs.
The launch article's district-targeting description is not a comparative local risk model. Historical tensions and proposed last-mile services do not establish a current climate-conflict trend.
